WASHINGTON – Today, Senator Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) sent a letter to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calling out the hypocrisy of Anthropic’s plans to IPO, tying millions of Americans’ hard earned dollars to the company’s success, while simultaneously claiming his technology could lead to human extinction. In his letter, Senator Moreno urged Mr. Amodei to follow the White House’s lead and focus on the ways that Super Intelligence (“SI”) can be used to improve the lives of Americans and defend against real, SI-enabled threats.

“These questions are even more consequential as Anthropic prepares to go public and invite millions of Americans to tie their financial futures to the development and success of your company’s technology,” wrote Senator Moreno. “With investors discussing a valuation approaching $2 trillion (about 42 times Anthropic’s revenue and double what the company was worth four months ago), and trading expected as soon as October 2026, Anthropic’s entrance into the public market will be one of the largest in history. While I applaud any company that gives hardworking Americans access to its success, I do not understand how you can ask them to invest their hard-earned savings in Anthropic’s continued development while warning those same Americans that your product could ultimately lead to their extinction.”

Read the full text of the letter HERE or below.

October 5, 2026

Mr. Dario Amodei

Chief Executive Officer

Anthropic PBC

548 Market Street

San Francisco, CA 94104

Dear Mr. Amodei,

Anthropic, PBC (“Anthropic”) maintains a leading presence in the Super Intelligence (“SI”) ecosystem. As Anthropic’s co-founder and a prominent public voice on SI, you, Mr. Amodei, are viewed by the American public and policymakers as one of the technology’s principal stewards. The systems Anthropic is developing could change the American way of life forever. With great power comes great responsibility, and in this case, I am concerned that you are failing to meet the moment.

Anthropic’s recent actions and statements reflect an alarmist approach to SI that places extraordinary emphasis on the technology’s most catastrophic outcomes. As you know, SI researcher Jacob Coxon recently quit his job at Anthropic and accused your company and its business rival, OpenAI, of “gambling with our lives.” Mr. Coxon publicized his exit on Twitter, claiming, “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt. If anything, many executives and senior researchers will couch their phrasing in the press to sound sensible – but I hear the same people express fear privately. No other human activity poses this level of danger.”

That same day, one of Anthropic’s top safety experts, Evan Hubinger, agreed with Mr. Coxon, tweeting, “Jacob is correct here—we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade.” A couple of days after these tweets, you appeared on CNN and said, “It’s funny, I agree with Jacob Coxon on far more than I disagree with him.” You have also been on the record as saying that there’s a twenty-five percent chance that developing SI further will go “really, really badly.” These statements, which include your own words, indicate that your instinct is to wreak havoc on the public SI discourse. Yet your panic-inducing commentary frames SI as an existential threat without providing information to the American people about how SI technology can also be used to combat and defend against the very safety threats you emphasize.

These questions are even more consequential as Anthropic prepares to go public and invite millions of Americans to tie their financial futures to the development and success of your company’s technology. With investors discussing a valuation approaching $2 trillion (about 42 times Anthropic’s revenue and double what the company was worth four months ago), and trading expected as soon as October 2026, Anthropic’s entrance into the public market will be one of the largest in history. While I applaud any company that gives hardworking Americans access to its success, I do not understand how you can ask them to invest their hard-earned savings in Anthropic’s continued development while warning those same Americans that your product could ultimately lead to their extinction.

I am equally concerned that this focus on potential catastrophic outcomes risks crowding out an equally important public debate: how American SI leadership can strengthen U.S. national security, counter SI-powered attacks from our adversaries, and ensure that the United States, not China, shapes the future of this technology. Rather than highlighting how SI could end humanity, public discourse around SI should focus on developing solutions to the real vulnerabilities SI has found in American critical infrastructure and cybersecurity. We should not unnecessarily metastasize SI ‘doomerism,’ but rather recognize that SI, like any cutting-edge technology, presents risks that must be addressed by companies who are able to rise to the occasion. I am sincerely hopeful you and your company will work to develop and propagate such solutions as opposed to publicly pontificating the worst-case scenario. Adding your signature to the White House Accord on Super Intelligence is a notable first step. I applaud President Trump’s unwavering commitment to American dominance in responsible SI development.

Public discourse around SI should center on how American innovators, working where appropriate with the U.S. government, can harness this technology to strengthen U.S. national security, improve the lives of American people, and position the country to respond to our adversaries’ increasingly sophisticated SI-enabled threats. We must address the risks associated with frontier SI. Doing so does not require halting its development or surrendering American technological dominance. It requires confronting those risks with the same ingenuity and creativity that have defined American innovation for generations.

matches.text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sen. Mark R. Warner (D-VA), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, released the following statement after President Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to serve in an additional role overseeing the administration’s artificial intelligence policy:

“Artificial intelligence is one of the defining national security challenges of our time, and I welcome the administration recognizing that this technology requires serious, sustained attention at the highest levels of government. But creating a new title is not a substitute for having a coherent strategy. So far, the administration has resisted meaningful safeguards without offering a serious alternative for addressing the national security risks posed by increasingly powerful AI systems. We still do not know what authority this new role will have, whether it will include developing safety standards or reviewing the most advanced models, or how it fits into the administration’s broader approach to AI. That lack of clarity is especially concerning as leading AI companies themselves are confronting increasingly capable systems that can evade safeguards and exploit cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

“There is real bipartisan interest in Congress in getting this right. I hope this appointment is an opportunity for the administration to move beyond slogans and toward a serious, coordinated national strategy for AI. As I have said repeatedly, that coordination must include the Intelligence Community, where some of our nation’s foremost technical experts on cyber reside. And as Vice Chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, I look forward to working with Director Clayton on ensuring the United States stays ahead of China and other adversaries, strengthening the security and resilience of our most advanced AI systems, and establishing rigorous testing and safeguards so that increasingly powerful systems remain secure, reliable, and under human control. ”

Sen. Warner has been a leading voice in Congress on the national security, economic, and societal implications of artificial intelligence. Earlier this year, he unveiled A Framework for America’s AI Future, a comprehensive legislative agenda focused on AI safety and competition, national security, workforce disruption, and the infrastructure needed to power the technology. Most recently, Warner introduced the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 with Sens. Brian Schatz (D-HI) and Andy Kim (D-NJ), legislation that would establish enforceable safety and security standards for the most advanced AI systems, including pre-deployment testing, stronger cybersecurity requirements, and mandatory reporting of serious AI safety and security incidents. Warner and his colleagues took to the Senate floor this week to seek unanimous consent to pass the legislation.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representative Sharice Davids, a member of the Build America Caucus, helped announce the Build More Agenda — a major bipartisan policy platform designed to fix federal gridlock, strengthen local economies, create jobs, and lower everyday prices for hardworking families. By streamlining approval processes for energy, housing, and infrastructure, the roadmap directly targets the bureaucratic delays that slow down construction, drive up utility and housing costs, and prevent critical projects from getting built.

“Kansans don’t want D.C. talking points — they want lower utility bills, homes they can actually afford, and roads that aren't falling apart,” said Davids. “The problem isn't a lack of good ideas; it's the bureaucratic red tape slowing projects down for years. I’m supporting the bipartisan Build America Caucus’ new agenda because it would help cut through government gridlock and start building these projects now, not a decade from now.”

The bipartisan Build America Caucus was established to give pro-growth, pragmatic policymaking a permanent foothold in Congress. Over the past year, the Caucus helped negotiate and pass major bipartisan housing reform legislation and led bipartisan efforts to deliver permitting certainty for energy and infrastructure projects. Spanning seven core policy areas and over 60 legislative proposals, the Build More Agenda builds on those successes, establishing a comprehensive framework to spur domestic production, bring manufacturing home, create good-paying jobs, and lower the cost of living for Kansans.

“Not enough homes or energy, shortages of doctors and daycares, cures that take too long to reach patients, and infrastructure projects that drag on for decades. That’s what life in America looks like today because we’ve lost the ability to build the things we need,” said CaucusCo-Chairs Harder and Maloy. “We used to believe that America was the only place in the world where the boldest dreams could be realized, and we need a new politics of action to restore that national ambition and trust in government. The Build America Caucus was founded a little over a year ago with that goal in mind, and the Build More Agenda is our bipartisan roadmap to make growth and prosperity the cornerstone of American life once again.”

The solution to systemic dysfunction is to build our way to prosperity:

Lowering Housing Costs: With the nation facing a shortage of five million homes, the agenda reduces regulatory delays, unlocks new project financing, and fully implements the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to expand homeownership options and bring housing prices back within reach for young families and working Kansans.

Cutting Healthcare Costs & Red Tape: We spend more on healthcare than any other nation, but that care is unaffordable, inaccessible, and archaic. It reallocates physician training investments and slashes mountain-high administrative paperwork, so doctors spend time on patient outcomes rather than bureaucracy — cutting health system waste and lowering out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.

Cheaper, Reliable Energy: Electricity rates have jumped more than 30 percent in recent years. The platform fixes broken permitting rules, so grid upgrades and energy projects don't take longer to approve than to actually construct, bringing down monthly electricity bills for households and small businesses.

Building Infrastructure Faster: It establishes dedicated fast-track approvals and smarter federal funding models to ensure roads, bridges, and water systems are completed on schedule and under budget — ending costly construction delays that waste taxpayer dollars.

Accelerating Medical Cures: America is losing its scientific edge because our scientists spend half their time on paperwork and research dollars aren’t geared toward modern discovery. It saves American medical researchers over one million hours a year spent on bureaucratic paperwork, redirecting resources toward breakthrough science and AI technology to accelerate cures for cancer, Alzheimer's, and chronic conditions.

Expanding Childcare & Workforce Pipelines: It strengthens workforce development programs that directly match workers to high-paying local jobs, while expanding accessible childcare options so parents can stay in the workforce without breaking their household budgets.

Modernizing Government to Save Taxpayer Dollars: It cuts redundant D.C. red tape, updates archaic federal technology systems, and builds a skill-focused public workforce that manages taxpayer funds efficiently.

Read the full agenda here. Read a section-by-section here.

“America knows how to build, we just have to get out of our own way and start doing it,” said Rep. Janelle Bynum (D-OR-05). “More homes, better roads and bridges, new technology, and good jobs – this agenda is about turning big ideas into things people can actually see and feel in their communities. I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and help get it done.”

“Americans are tired of Washington making it harder and more expensive to build, innovate, and grow,” said Rep. Buddy Carter (R-GA-01). “The Build More Agenda brings Republicans and Democrats together around commonsense solutions to cut red tape, lower costs, strengthen American energy, improve access to healthcare, and get critical projects built. I’m proud to work with the Build America Caucus to turn good ideas into real results for the American people.”

“The Build More Agenda reflects what we can accomplish when we work across the aisle to tackle challenges facing American families and businesses,” said Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12). “I’m proud to join my colleagues in the bipartisan Build America Caucus to advance practical solutions that cut unnecessary red tape, lower costs, and help America build faster and smarter. By modernizing infrastructure and creating opportunities for American workers and manufacturers, we can strengthen our economy, make taxpayer dollars go further, and deliver lasting results for our communities.”

“America used to pride itself on accomplishing big things — winning world wars, sending man to the moon, or discovering the next medical breakthrough,” said Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA-50). “Today, our challenges have not gone away, but our capacity to achieve great things has. Our constituents are counting on us to put politics aside and invest in our country’s future to make their lives better. The bipartisan Build More Agenda includes ways to do exactly that: lower costs, create good-paying jobs, strengthen communities, and restore America as a global leader in progress and innovation.”

“Folks in Western and Southern Colorado know how to build things, create jobs, and get things done,” said Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-03). “Too often, Washington just gets in the way. The Build More Agenda is about cutting unnecessary red tape so we can produce more American energy, build the housing and infrastructure our communities need, and bring down costs for working families. Republicans and Democrats aren’t going to agree on everything, but we ought to be able to agree that it shouldn’t take years of paperwork and bureaucracy to build something in this country.”

“A housing shortage is a tax on working people, and they pay it every month in rent,” said Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15). “For decades, we have piled on rules and caps that make it slower and costlier to build homes, and few places have paid a higher price than the Bronx. The surest way to bring down the cost of housing is to bring up the supply of housing. The Build More Agenda is built on that principle, because a pro-growth agenda is a pro–working class agenda. Progress should be measured not by how many projects we regulate but by how many we deliver.”

“Congress passed a housing abundance bill this term,” said Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA-04). “It's seriously debating a bipartisan energy abundance bill. Build America has momentum in its mission to lower prices by building more, faster & better – next up are unlocks to lower prices in medicine, transportation, and childcare.”

“As a senior member of the Housing, Transportation, and Urban Development Subcommittee, I’m proud to be a member of the bipartisan Build America Caucus. My constituents tell me every day they want to see their representatives in Washington take actions that will make their lives better – lower the cost of housing, healthcare, and energy,” said Rep. Mike Quigley (D-IL-05). “At a time of deep political division, we have the unique opportunity to come together as Democrats and Republicans to lower costs and solve the housing crisis.”

“Whether it’s rebuilding a bridge over I-95 in record time or passing landmark housing legislation, we know that government can still get things done, if rarely,” said Rep. Jim Himes (D-CT-04). “I’m in the Build America Caucus because this group of lawmakers fundamentally believes government needs to get things done — not as the exception, but as the rule. Our agenda reflects that belief, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to turn our group’s governing principle into law.”

What they’re saying about the Build More Agenda:

“For too long, we’ve treated a four-year college degree as the default path to a good career. The Build America Caucus’s push to get more apprenticeships and higher-quality workforce training programs off the ground is a critical step forward. If we want to build more in America, we need to make it easier for more Americans to learn how to do the building,” said Zach Boren, Senior Vice President, Apprenticeships for America.

“Getting lawmakers from both parties to agree on what's holding the country back is no easy feat, and we applaud the Build America Caucus for assembling a genuinely bipartisan coalition around these questions. BPC Action has long argued that the problems on this list — the cost of building housing, the time it takes to approve energy projects, and a broken childcare system — are solvable ones. We look forward to working with the caucus and its members as they move from agenda to legislation,” said Michele Stockwell, President, BPC Action.

“Through their work with the Build America Caucus, Reps. Harder and Maloy have asked how we can build more of what Americans actually need and answered it across housing, childcare, energy, and more. We applaud this effort and its goal to build 5 million homes, add millions more new childcare slots, modernize the energy grid, and get infrastructure built faster. This comprehensive plan demonstrates that pragmatic, actionable solutions can still be ambitious. This Agenda, written by a Democrat from California and a Republican from Utah, also shows the strength of abundance solutions in building coalitions. I urge Congress to take action on these solutions,” said Derek Kaufman, President, Inclusive Abundance Action.

“The Build More Agenda is an innovative, bipartisan framework for creating a more abundant future in America. The priorities laid out in this agenda have the potential to make a massive difference in areas from science and innovation to housing, transportation, and energy. For example, we were thrilled to see X-Labs and metascience units highlighted as vehicles to accelerate scientific discovery and increase the return on investment for R&D. Similarly, the Agenda’s focus on reducing land use regulations, building transit at lower cost, and achieving energy abundance is crucial for letting America build again and innovate in the world of atoms,” said Alec Stapp, CEO, Institute for Progress.

“For the past year, the Build America Caucus has worked across the aisle to notch key policy wins, making it easier, cheaper, and faster to build in America. The Build More Agenda strengthens that foundation, with over sixty policy proposals covering seven different policy areas. NAIA looks forward to working with the Caucus to back the builders,” said the New America Industrial Alliance.

“Finding childcare that's both affordable and meets their family’s specific needs is nearly impossible for far too many American parents. This agenda from the Build America Caucus offers an innovative menu of reforms to identify and remove the barriers to a more abundant supply of childcare options that fit family preferences without sacrificing quality or safety,” said Josh McCabe, Director of Social Policy, Niskanen Center.

“The housing affordability crisis is the result of many different factors, and solving it requires an all-hands-on-deck approach. The Build America Caucus agenda delivers this, with solutions that make it easier and less expensive to build housing. Critically, it does the same for transportation infrastructure and buses, because abundant housing and effective transportation options work together to connect people to economic opportunity,” said Kimberly Burnett, Deputy Director of Housing and Transportation, Niskanen Center.

“America's healthcare affordability crisis is fueled by a scarce and consolidated supply side of the market. This agenda from the Build America Caucus rightly targets solutions that increase care availability and cut out the incentives that drive consolidation,” said Lawson Mansell, Senior Health Policy Analyst, Niskanen Center.

“We applaud the Build America Caucus for its energy agenda focused on more power and lower bills. Getting transmission right and having neighboring regions connected is how you build a grid Americans can afford,” said Sarah Iskander, Government Affairs Manager, Niskanen Center.

“Whether it's housing, transportation, energy, or infrastructure, the federal government needs the tools and capacity to deliver for the American people. Meeting those demands requires a government whose systems and processes make delivery possible, and right now ours is not built to keep pace with changes in the workforce, technology, and the public's needs. The Build America Caucus's policy agenda takes this challenge head-on, rightly recognizing state capacity as essential to unlocking a prosperous future for our country,” said Max Stier, President and CEO, Partnership for Public Service.

PENN HILLS, PA – Yesterday, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) kicked off his October Town Hall Tour with an event open to the public and the press in Penn Hills, Pennsylvania. A large group of Western Pennsylvanians joined him for the first stop of the Town Hall Tour in Pennsylvania’s 17th District.

Constituents had an opportunity to speak directly with their elected representative in Congress, share their opinions, and ask questions. “A lot has happened down in Washington this year, and it is good to be home to hear from the people that Congress’s work impacts the most,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Folks in Penn Hills want to know how we can fight the cost-of-living crisis, end the President’s reckless war in Iran, and restore the American Dream right here in Western Pennsylvania. WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Chris Coons (D-Del.) and Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.) introduced the Strategic Technology and Resilient Alliances (STRATA) Act, bipartisan legislation to strengthen U.S. and allied critical minerals supply chains by accelerating innovation and developing new technologies at every stage of mining and refining critical minerals. Representatives Young Kim (R-Calif.) and Ami Bera (D-Calif.) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

“China’s critical mineral dominance poses a challenge the U.S. cannot address through traditional mining and processing alone,” said Senator Coons. “The STRATA Act would use America’s advantages in innovation and our strong ties with partners and allies around the world to secure our critical mineral infrastructure. By working with our allies to advance new technologies, build technical capacity, and strengthen supply chains, we can expand access to critical minerals and protect our national security.”

“America is a nation of innovation. As we race to counter China’s dominance of critical minerals and secure our supply chain, we must maintain our competitive edge with new technological advances that can expedite the delivery of new critical mineral sources, reduce our dependency on foreign adversaries, and protect our national security,” said Senator Sheehy.“The STRATA Act will accelerate breakthroughs in extraction, processing, recycling, recovery, and advanced materials, working with our allies to build resilient supply chains and keep America at the forefront of critical-minerals innovation.”

“The Chinese Communist Party has spent decades cornering the market on critical minerals and using supply chains as a tool of economic coercion,” said Rep. Kim. “We cannot wait another moment to address this challenge. The STRATA Act plays to America’s greatest strengths: innovation and our strong alliances. By launching a Critical Mineral Innovation Initiative at the State Department, sharing technology with allies, and expanding domestic recycling, we will build a secure supply chain faster and smarter. I’m proud to partner with Senator Coons in the Senate to get this bill signed into law, because economic security is national security, and the STRATA Act delivers both.”

Critical minerals are essential to advanced technologies, energy infrastructure, semiconductors, and defense systems, but critical minerals supply chains remain heavily concentrated in China. The United States has made significant investments in expanding domestic mining and processing, including recent federal investments in new mining technologies, mineral recovery, and processing capacity.

The STRATA Act would complement those efforts by making innovation and international collaboration a central part of the U.S. critical minerals strategy. The legislation would establish formal partnerships with trusted allies to accelerate the development and deployment of advanced extraction and processing technologies, mineral substitution, recycling, recovery from waste streams, and new materials.

The STRATA Act would:

Establish a Critical Minerals Innovation Partnership Program at the State Department to coordinate U.S. and allied strategies, develop joint research and innovation initiatives, and support partnerships with universities, national laboratories, nonprofits, and industry

Create International Centers of Excellence at academic institutions to advance research, technical assistance, workforce development, and long-term partnerships across the critical minerals supply chain

Launch a public digital platform serving as a centralized clearinghouse for funding opportunities, solicitations, and collaborative research, while creating pathways for startups and emerging companies to participate

Connect innovation to commercialization and national security by coordinating with federal agencies, financing institutions, the National Science and Technology Council, and the National Defense Technology and Industrial Base Council to help move promising technologies from research and development ultimately into deployment

Strengthen supply chain safeguards and transparency by establishing standards for data security, sensitive technologies, supply chain transparency, monitoring, and verification, while limiting participation by countries and entities of concern

Build long-term allied capacity through technical assistance, joint research, shared infrastructure, and cooperation on environmental, labor, and human rights standards

The STRATA Act would authorize these partnerships for 10 years and require congressional notification before establishing new partnerships. The legislation would also prohibit partnerships with countries of concern and entities of concern.

“The STRATA Act represents forward-thinking policy that the United States needs to maintain its technological edge and its leadership on science diplomacy,” said Daniel Correa, Chief Executive Officer of the Federation of American Scientists. “Structured partnerships with our allies on critical minerals innovation can ensure that the best science and the best talent are working together towards shared security and economic prosperity.”

“Engaging earlier and in-depth on critical technologies that will shape our collective futures is a statecraft imperative for liberal democracies globally. I’m delighted to see this Committee and the Legislative Branch recognizing and acting to drive a leadership role for the US and the DoS. Now is absolutely the time!” said Dawn Meyerriecks, former director of the Directorate of Science and Technology at the Central Intelligence Agency.

“Increasing the legibility of existing investments, agreements, and supplies of critical minerals can surface information for policymakers and private investors focused on securing supply chains,” said Joshua Levine, director, Technology & Statecraft, Foundation for American Innovation (*affiliation for identification only). “STRATA works to do this, within a defined timeline, and should be seen as a positive step toward loosening chokepoints for inputs critical to American innovation and next-generation technologies.”

“STRATA is a well-timed and strongly bipartisan effort to tackle one of the most important national security challenges of the day — how to ensure that the growing demand for critical minerals to power our defense systems, energy transition and the infrastructure to support America’s lead in the AI revolution does not strengthen China’s already strong position in these supply chains,” said Geoff Pyatt, Ambassador (ret.), senior managing director of Energy and Critical Minerals at McLarty Associates. “The State Department — and the energy security team that I was honored to lead — has worked closely with the Congressional foreign affairs leadership to make sure that America’s national security toolkit is fit for purpose on these issues. And China has already demonstrated in repeated instances its willingness to weaponize its market dominance in these sectors for strategic advantage. I applaud Senator Coons and his Senate colleagues for focusing SFRC attention on this critical line of effort.”

“America and our allies have the ingenuity and industrial base to lead the world in critical minerals mining and processing,” said ClearPath Action CEO Jeremy Harrell. “The STRATA Act puts these advantages to work and funds the joint research needed to surpass China and secure the supply chain that next-generation energy technologies rely on.”

“The STRATA Act takes a smart, forward-looking approach to securing the critical minerals our economy depends on, investing in the researchers and entrepreneurs developing new ways to produce, recycle, and replace these materials. NAIA supports this bill and thanks Senators Coons and Sheehy for their leadership,” said a representative from the New American Industrial Alliance.

Read the full text of the STRATA Act here.

Washington, D.C. – In case you missed it, during the final weeks of the September Senate session, U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) successfully championed several key pieces of legislation through the Senate, delivering progress on priorities for New Mexico and communities across the country. Delivering for New Mexico’s Land Grant Communities and Traditional Uses: Senator Luján led the unanimous Senate passage of the New Mexico Land Grant-Mercedes Historical or Traditional Use Cooperation and Coordination Act, legislation to strengthen cooperation between the federal government and land grant communities.

Washington (October 6, 2026) - Senators Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), members of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works, this week sent a letter opposing the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) proposal to eliminate the 30-day mandatory public notice period that allows communities to provide input on proposed facilities, like data centers, that may affect the air they breathe.

“We agree that permitting should be efficient, predictable, and capable of supporting the infrastructure our country needs. But faster permitting should not come at the expense of transparency or communities’ ability to shape the decisions that affect them,” wrote the senators to Administrator Zeldin.

The letter to the EPA was co-signed by Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.).

Read the full letter to the EPA here.

The proposed rollback is included in the Senator’s recent report, The EPA’s Data Center Disaster: How the Trump Administration is Destroying Environmental Protections and Selling Out Communities for Big Tech, which details the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)’s campaign of reckless deregulation to dilute environmental and public health guardrails in direct service of Big Tech’s race to build data centers.

Senator Markey has been a leading voice against irresponsible and unregulated data center buildout at the expense of public health and the environment.

In July, Senator Markey released a discussion draft of his Protecting Communities Against Data Center Impacts proposal, a bill that would create a national framework to prevent increased energy costs, pollution, and adverse health harms related to the rapid buildout of data centers and associated fossil fuel infrastructure.

In June, Senator Markey wrote to EPA Administrator Zeldin to demand the withdrawal of a proposed rule that underminesClean Air Act permitting standards to facilitate the buildout of data centers and associated fossil fuel infrastructure.

In June, Senator Markey reintroduced his Artificial Intelligence (AI) Environmental Impacts Act, legislation that would require data center operators to report the full range of their facilities’ environmental impacts.

In November 2025, Senator Markey wrote to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) urging the agency to ensure that increased and projected energy demand from data centers does not result in unjust or unreasonable rate hikes for American households.

In September 2025, Senator Markey wrote to the EPA in opposition to the agency’s initial announcement of plans to roll back the NSR program for data center buildout.

In July 2025, Senator Markey hosted a roundtable discussion titled The Data Center Next Door: Hidden Costs and Harms of Artificial Intelligence and Cryptomining to highlight the adverse environmental, health, climate, and energy cost impacts of data center proliferation in communities across the United States, and to condemn the deregulatory actions set forth in President Trump’s AI Action Plan. On the day of the roundtable, Senator Markey also released a storybook to spotlight the experiences of American families living with data centers in their backyard.

WASHINGTON – Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, joined Rep. André Carson (D-IN), Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA), Rep. Paul Tonko (D-NY), and Rep. Mike Levin (D-CA), to raise serious concerns about the Department of Energy’s decision to abandon three proposed National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors (NIETCs), warning that the move could undermine U.S. manufacturing, increase electricity costs for American families, and weaken the nation’s ability to compete with China.

In a [democrats-selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/sites/evo-subsites/democrats-selectcommitteeontheccp.house.gov/files/evo-media-document/2026.10.06-letter-to-doe-on-nietc-cancellations.pdf]letter to Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Tuesday, the lawmakers questioned the Department’s August 12 decision not to move forward with the Lake Erie-Canada Corridor, Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor, and Tribal Energy Access Corridor. He also pressed the Department to explain how it plans to address the nation’s urgent transmission needs and accelerate permitting for critical grid infrastructure.

The letter comes as the Department’s own July 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study found a “pressing need” for additional transmission infrastructure driven in part by expanding domestic manufacturing, large industrial loads, data centers, and a growing economy.

“Arbitrary cancellations like these set back the U.S. in the strategic race with the CCP, hamstring a U.S. manufacturing buildout, and drive up costs for American families,” the lawmakers wrote.

The Members further raised concerns about the impact of inadequate transmission capacity on American consumers. As electricity rates continue to rise, transmission constraints are driving up wholesale power costs and limit the ability of regions to bring new generation online, putting additional pressure on families and businesses already struggling with higher energy bills, the lawmakers wrote.

The Members are calling on Secretary Wright to provide detailed answers to the following by October 26, 2026:

Please provide a detailed account of any analysis conducted by the Department of the opportunity cost of cancelling the Lake Erie–Canada Corridor, the Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor, and the Tribal Energy Access Corridor, including projected effects on ratepayer costs, grid reliability, and industrial electricity supply in the affected regions.

Did the Department assess the impact of these cancellations on potential manufacturing and energy-intensive development in the regions associated with these cancelled corridors? Please provide a detailed account of that analysis.

How does the Department reconcile these cancellations with the findings of its own July 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study?

What stakeholder feedback did the Department evaluate when deciding to cancel these NIETC designations and did the Department engage with utilities, regional transmission organizations, or the North American Electric Reliability Corporation?

What steps, if any, will the Department take to address the transmission needs in these three corridors, or in other transmission constrained areas across the country (especially those identified in the 2026 draft National Transmission Needs Study)?

Read the full letter to Energy Secretary Wright HERE.

Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, released a discussion draft of the Clear Liability for Artificial Intelligence Misconduct (CLAIM) Act. The legislation would give those harmed by AI agents a clear path to recovery by holding developers responsible when their systems engage in conduct that would be unlawful if committed by a person.

“When someone breaks the law and hurts you, you can take them to court. That shouldn't change just because the wrongdoer is an AI agent,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “Developers have already built systems capable of acting on their own and causing real damage. The CLAIM Act makes sure they answer for what their systems do.”

Specifically, the CLAIM Act:

Holds developers liable for AI misconduct. If an AI system injures a third party through conduct that would constitute negligence, an intentional tort, or a crime if committed by a person, the developer is liable. Liability does not apply where the user or a company that modified the system intended the conduct or was negligent.

Resolves uncertainty around AI and intent. Courts would presume an AI system acted with the state of mind a person taking the same actions would have had. Developers could not argue that AI is incapable of intent.

Establishes a federal cause of action. Injured parties may bring claims in federal or state court.

Preserves state law. The bill sets a federal floor and does not preempt any state law. Existing state claims and state AI laws remain fully available.

The risks the CLAIM Act addresses already exist. In July, AI agents undergoing an evaluation by OpenAI escaped their test environment and hacked into Hugging Face, another AI company. No one instructed them to do so. Leading experts have called the incident a warning shot for a future of increasingly capable AI agents acting outside their users’ control.

Under current law, third parties harmed by a misaligned AI agent face significant hurdles. Many serious harms, including hacking and fraud, require proof of intent, and courts have not settled whether an AI system’s conduct can meet that standard. Negligence and product liability claims typically require showing that a company failed to take a specific precaution or ignored a safer design. Because AI alignment remains an unsolved technical problem, developers can argue the harm occurred despite their best efforts, leaving injured parties without a remedy.

The CLAIM Act complements the bipartisan FRONTIER Act, which Trahan introduced with Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA) to address catastrophic risks from the most advanced AI models. FRONTIER establishes transparency, independent verification, and incident reporting requirements. The CLAIM Act adds a robust liability regime that rewards developers who invest in making their systems safer.

Trahan is releasing the CLAIM Act as a discussion draft and welcomes feedback from experts, industry, advocates, and the public. In addition to comments on the draft legislation, the office welcomes answers to important questions related to the CLAIM Act and AI liability located HERE.

Comments can be submitted to MA03Leg@mail.house.gov.

A copy of the bill text can be accessed HERE.

matches.text:
Labor, energy producers, and nonprofits voice strong support for Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Since four Senators from across the political spectrum introduced their Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act last week, a broad coalition of labor leaders, energy producers, and nonprofits has voiced support for the permitting reform plan, noting that it will deliver cheaper energy, more jobs, and responsible growth. The legislation was drafted by U.S. Senators Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee; Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources (ENR) Committee; Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Ranking Member of the EPW Committee; and Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the ENR Committee.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act delivers cheaper energy, more well-paying jobs, and responsible growth by accelerating the permitting and construction of critical energy and infrastructure projects while maintaining key environmental and historic preservation safeguards. The legislation provides greater certainty for projects that have already been permitted and financed, including by preventing future administrations from arbitrarily blocking entire classes of energy projects, while establishing clear timelines for environmental reviews and legal challenges. It also includes targeted reforms to expand and modernize the electric grid, speed the development of geothermal and other energy projects, and ensure that rapidly growing data centers pay the full cost of their associated transmission needs rather than passing those costs on to families and small businesses. The legislation reflects input from members of Congress on both sides of the aisle and a diverse group of stakeholders.

The bill text is available here.

Labor

“For LIUNA, the key consideration is whether a permitting package will translate to good union jobs, with prevailing wages and robust apprenticeship opportunities. S.5653 exceeds those standards while maintaining proper regulations and safeguards that protect both our members on the job as well as the local communities in which projects take place. Moreover, it will lower energy costs for all Americans at a time when prices of everyday living expenses are at an all-time high,” said LIUNA General President Brent Booker. “For more than a decade LIUNA has testified before Congress, submitted comments, participated in roundtables, and endorsed numerous iterations of permitting bills only to see every effort and attempt fail in final hours of the congressional calendar. Congress has another opportunity to get this done. We urge lawmakers in both parties to seize this moment, pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, and finally deliver meaningful permitting reform. It is time to stop making permitting reform the Groundhog Day of Congress.”

“In our industry, uncertainty means one thing: unemployment. It is long past time that Congress enacts meaningful permitting reform to put UA members to work faster delivering reliable and affordable energy to American communities. Today’s announcement is the culmination of a long process to reach a bipartisan deal and take a critical step towards a long-overdue modernization of our country’s permitting process. This bipartisan legislation, led by Chairs Lee and Capito and Ranking Members Heinrich and Whitehouse, will increase project certainty, streamline federal review timelines, and create thousands of good-paying jobs – all while maintaining reasonable environmental safeguards and opportunities for public input. The UA looks forward to continuing our work with members of both parties in the Senate to advance this critical legislation and with all members in the House to ultimately pass it into law,” said United Association of Union Plumbers and Pipefitters (UA) General President Mark McManus.

“We have seen too many projects unnecessarily delayed for years through litigation, and other projects abandoned by contractors or terminated by the federal government because of our nation’s antiquated permitting process. As a result, thousands of good-paying union jobs have been lost, and taxpayers have been deprived of safer infrastructure and more affordable energy,” said John L. Downey, General President of the International Union of Operating Engineers. “Passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will result in building energy transmission capacity faster, delivering more energy to the grid, creating greater certainty for projects permitted and financed across administrations, and setting clear deadlines for environmental reviews. These reforms will put thousands of Operating Engineers to work, along with other highly skilled crafts people, while making energy more affordable and reliable for American families.”

Nonprofits

“If America is going to meaningfully reduce our emissions and truly address climate change, we need to connect much more clean energy to the grid,” said Citizens Climate Lobby’s Executive Director Ricky Bradley. “This bill will make remarkable, rapid progress toward that goal. We’re proud to endorse it, and we’re excited to mobilize our grassroots volunteers in full support.”

“For decades, the Club for Growth has championed deregulation and permitting reform. We commend President Trump and Senate leaders for moving this agreement forward with legislative text. These reforms are critical to expanding American energy production and lowering energy costs for families and businesses. Excessive regulation has constrained production and contributed to higher costs for American consumers. We urge the Senate andHouse to act swiftly and pass these important permitting reforms,” said David McIntosh, President, Club for Growth.

“The Climate Leadership Council is encouraged by progress on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. Council analysis projects U.S. electricity demand to grow nearly 60% by 2050, and meeting that demand will require building energy infrastructure faster than our current system allows. Permitting reform is essential to keep pace with the demands of a modern economy, and the energy infrastructure it unlocks is what drives clean energy deployment and innovation. CLC looks forward to continued engagement with stakeholders and policymakers as the bill moves forward,” said Erin Alejandre, Director of Policy at the Climate Leadership Council.

“On behalf of grassroots activists across the country, we strongly applaud theintroduction of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). Your work over much of this Congress to negotiate the details and make a bipartisan package a reality is a major step forward for the American people and for our energy, technological, and national future,” said Brent Gardner, Chief Government Affairs Officer, Americans for Prosperity.

“After years of working toward this goal, lawmakers from both parties have reached a deal to fix the broken system that keeps America from building the power plants and power lines that would bring costs down. This is a huge bipartisan win at a moment when our politics has made wins like this rare,”said Inclusive Abundance Action President Derek Kaufman. “Families are paying too much for electricity because new energy projects wait years on government reviews, then years more in court, and even once they clear, partisan politics can still take them out. That scarcity is a choice. Today, Congress is choosing differently.”

“The need for reform is one of the few things Republicans and Democrats agree on, and these Senate leaders have translated that consensus into a comprehensive, bipartisan bill. Permitting reform cannot wait, and the time to act is now,”said Michele Stockwell, president of Bipartisan Policy Center Action. “BPC Action has long argued that durable permitting reform must be bipartisan, technology-neutral, and maintain strong environmental standards. We urge swift action and look forward to working with members of both parties to get this bill to the president’s desk this Congress.”

“Pacific Legal Foundation strongly supports the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026,” said John Nagle, federal policy manager at Pacific Legal Foundation. “Americans should not have to navigate years of costly and unpredictable government processes simply to build a home, develop new energy resources, or create the infrastructure our communities need. Reforming our permitting system is essential to removing unnecessary government barriers that delay projects, drive up costs, and discourage investment. We encourage Congress to move quickly to pass this bill to lower costs for Americans, protect property rights, and restore America’s ability to build.”

“Today, one of America’s most important supply lines is its electric grid, and we are not building it fast enough to meet the moment. Our military installations depend on the same civilian grid as every American household. When a transmission line takes a decade or more to approve, that is not just an economic problem. It is a strategic vulnerability, and our adversaries are not waiting years to build. This bill addresses that vulnerability. It sets firm deadlines on environmental reviews, speeds approvals for the transmission lines and power projects the country needs, and gives the federal government tools to move interstate power lines forward when they stall. Just as important, it ensures that once a project is permitted, no administration can revoke it for political reasons. At the same time, it preserves the government's ability to act in the face of a genuine safety or national security threat, and it keeps reasonable environmental safeguards and opportunities for public input in place. That kind of certainty matters for every form of American energy, including the clean energy that will power our future,” said Major General Paul D. Eaton, U.S. Army (Ret.), Senior Advisor at VoteVets.

“[The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act] is better than I could have expected. Sens. Capito (R-WV), Heinrich (D-NM), Lee (R-UT), and Whitehouse (D-RI) negotiated a compromise bill where each side got real, meaningful wins. This bill would fix our permitting processes so that we can review and build efficiently, reducing costs, improving quality of life, growing our economy, and improving economic outcomes. It’s truly a win-win. I’m optimistic that this incredible bill can be signed into law this year,” said Xan Fishman, Vice President, Energy, Bipartisan Policy Center.

“Permitting reform has stalled for years because Democrats feared losing environmental protections and Republicans feared a deal that would only help renewables. Sens. Heinrich, Lee, Capito and Whitehouse have shown there is a bargain that works for both sides,” said Colin Mortimer, Senior Director of Partnerships at the Progressive Policy Institute. “This bill would get power lines, clean energy and critical infrastructure built faster and lower costs for families while keeping strong safeguards in place.”

“If you care about decarbonizing the economy or reshoring American manufacturing, or cutting bills for ratepayers, then you should support this bill. No agreement is perfect, but there’s something in this permitting reform agreement that will, on net, benefit everybody. And there isn’t a better deal out there,” said Jane Flegal and Pavan Venkatakrishnan of the Searchlight Institute.

This legislation will help accelerate the process to bring critical infrastructure projects online, supporting the investments required to enhance reliability for our customers, reduce costs, and create new economic opportunities in the states we serve. Congress should pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 now,” said American Electric Power (AEP) Chairman, President and CEO Bill Fehrman.

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 represents an historic opportunity to modernize the grid and meet customers’ electricity demand with reliable, affordable power. If enacted into law, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 would safeguard critical environmental standards while providing greater process certainty for environmental reviews and ensure that the customers we serve benefit from our nation’s diverse energy resources. It will also unlock trillions of dollars in private sector investment and job creation to expedite the construction of critically needed energy infrastructure,” said Mark Hewett, President and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway Energy.

Heinrich on their leadership. We encourage Congress to build on this progress and to prioritize these critical reforms,”said Heather O’Neill, President and CEO of Advanced Energy United.

We applaud the work that has been done to date and urge Congress to pass commonsense, much-needed reforms that will benefit all Americans,” said Rich Nolan, President and CEO of the National Mining Association.

Reform will help grow our economy, reduce costs, and improve quality of life for all Americans,” said Brian Tatum, CEO of the National Governors Association.

“Counties are on the front lines of delivering the energy, water and transportation infrastructure projects that residents depend on,” said National Association of Counties Executive Director Matthew Chase. “The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act recognizes counties as cooperating agencies in federal environmental protection statutes. This legislation would modernize the federal permitting process, reduce unnecessary delays, accelerate project delivery and ensure local expertise is incorporated into federal decision-making. Counties applaud Senators Lee, Heinrich, Capito and Whitehouse for their leadership and urge Congress to advance this bipartisan permitting reform package.”

“Unfortunately, outdated federal bureaucracy continues to delay critical energy and infrastructure projects and drive up costs for hardworking families at a time when speed and efficiency matter most. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is an opportunity to change that. By bringing greater certainty and accountability to the permitting process, we can unleash American energy dominance, strengthen our grid, bring manufacturing and investment back home, and ensure the United States leads the next generation of economic growth,” said 21 governors in a statement.

matches.text:
“Saving the Middle Class and Restoring the American Dream” details five pillars of the senator’s economic policy plan

WASHINGTON — Today, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) released his sweeping economic policy plan to rebuild America’s middle class. The five-pillar plan, “Saving the Middle Class and Restoring the American Dream,” includes a tax on data centers and AI, a New-Deal style public service jobs program, and raising the minimum wage to $20-per-hour to build an economy by-and-for the middle class — not the elites.

“For far too long, we’ve had a broken economy where hard work just isn’t nearly enough. The federal government let giant corporations, billionaires, and elites write the rules, and we’re living with the results: costs have soared, wages have stalled, and jobs have left. This bipartisan, failed status quo must end,” said Senator Gallego. “Working-class Americans aren’t asking for handouts. They don’t resent anyone else’s success — they just want a fair system. Work hard enough, and you should be able to get ahead, provide for your kids, take a vacation, and even get rich.”

Pillar 1, titled “Raise Wages and Improve Benefits,” outlines the senator’s plan to bring the American Dream back within reach by:

Moving to sectoral bargaining and increasing union membership: The senator wants to move beyond the PRO Act and toward sectoral bargaining. Senator Gallego is the among the first Democrats to call for sectoral bargaining and is the first politician to state that it should be the goal of the U.S. government to triple union density by 2035.

Raising the minimum wage to $20-per-hour and require companies to pay double for overtime work — not time-and-a-half.

Cracking down on worker misclassification by ending the ability of employers, like Uber and DoorDash, to misclassify employees as “independent contractors” to skirt minimum wage, overtime, unemployment insurance, and workers’ compensation responsibilities.

Creating an Office of Worker Empowerment and Office of Worker Advocacy: Sen. Gallego is the first federal politician to call for the creation of these offices.

Pillar 2, titled “Create and Protect Quality Blue Collar Jobs” would safeguard and grow job opportunity by:

Creating a trade policy for the working class by:

Repealing President Trump’s reckless, across-the-board global tariffs and ending his trade war with Canada.

Pursuing a strategic trade policy targeting unfair practices by chronic-surplus countries like China.

Combining trade and other industrial policies to effectively grow domestic industry.

Creating an Industrial Policy Council at the Executive Office of the President: Similar to the National Security Council, the plan calls for the creation of an entity to coordinate government industrial policy initiatives and ensure all efforts reflect worker-first, community-first growth.

Pillar 3, titled “Restoring Worker Trust in Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence” would ensure workers have a voice in how AI shapes the workforce and get a fair share of the prosperity it creates by:

Creating a New-Deal style public service jobs program: The program would fund jobs that allow AI-displaced workers to serve the public, funded by taxing AI. Sen. Gallego is one of the first Democrats to call for a large-scale public jobs program.

Requiring industry and workers to negotiate over AI: Sen. Gallego is among the first politicians to propose this idea. This approach mirrors the way in which actors and writers negotiated with Hollywood after the strike in 2023 over AI, guaranteeing workers have a seat at the table.

Creating a corporate “robot” tax to discourage job dislocation and maintain company payroll contributions for automated-away jobs.

Pillar 4, titled “Expand Job-Creating Entrepreneurship, Focusing Outside of Superstar Cities” would grow Main Street communities by:

Creating a data center tax:Senator Gallego is calling for a 10% excise tax on data centers and for the removal of many data center tax breaks like bonus depreciation and deductions for state and local taxes. Specifically, Senator Gallego is calling on data centers to benefit communities by:

Using excise tax revenue to fund community investments.

Requiring data centers to cover the full cost of needed generation, transmission, and distribution upgrades to the grid rather than shifting costs to families and businesses.

Requiring data centers to bring additional energy to the grid, preventing energy cost increases for consumers and creating new production jobs —and require them to sustain energy investments even if they abandon the project.

Preventing data centers from using key chips and components from China to spur domestic manufacturing.

Pushing data centers to pay high wages and use union labor.

Protecting small businesses from giant corporations by modernizing and enforcing antitrust laws.

Pillar 5, titled “Help Workers Find Jobs Faster” would improve the job search process by:

Cracking down on fake job postings known as “ghost jobs,” prohibiting companies from posting job advertisements that they have no intention of actually filling.

Giving laid-off workers more time to find a new job: The plan calls for requiring companies to provide affected workers with 120-day notice in the event of a mass layoff or closure. Currently, the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act only requires companies to give employees 60-day notice.

ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. — U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, appeared on CNN’s The Lead with Jake Tapper today where he discussed his landmark legislation that will hold data centers accountable for the costs they impose on the electricity grid, helping to ensure families and small businesses aren’t stuck footing the bill. Heinrich also discussed reports of a deadly illness at a research facility in Russia.

“In the permitting bill, that we just released text on a little over a week ago, we mandate that [data centers] have to pay for both the electricity and for any grid upgrades. And we prohibit passing those costs along to average ratepayers, be those residential customers or small businesses,” said Heinrich.

VIDEO: U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, discusses with CNN’s Jake Tapper his landmark legislation that will hold data centers accountable for the costs they impose on the electric grid and reports of a suspected plague exposure at a research facility in Russia, October 7, 2026.

On Heinrich’s Bill to Make Data Centers Pay their Fair Share of Grid Costs:

Jake Tapper: “Senator, you're also the top Democrat on the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee. And I don't need to tell you the debate over data centers is huge — especially on your Committee. You're pushing to make data center owners pay for the electricity that their buildings require, and not families who live nearby. How would you do that?”

Senator Heinrich: “Well, actually, in the permitting bill, that we just released text on a little over a week ago, we mandate that [data centers] have to pay for both the electricity and for any grid upgrades. And we prohibit passing those costs along to average ratepayers, be those residential customers or small businesses.”

For more information on Heinrich’s landmark legislation to require data centers to fully pay for costs they create, click here.

On Reports of a Deadly Illness at a Research Facility in Russia:

Heinrich: “We have a long history of Russia kind of coloring outside the lines, going all the way back to the Soviet Union. I would be very concerned if this were an engineered pathogen. I don't have any unique information saying that is the case. But if it were the case, that would be cause for alarm. And, you know, one of the things that I think is incredibly important that's related is just the fact that we have a CDC right now in the United States that is sort of running on fumes. Between the Trump administration and the actions of DOGE here a little over a year ago, the CDC is just simply not the agency that it should be for things like surveillance for any kind of international pathogen. And so, I'm not going to add fuel to that fire, but certainly I would be deeply concerned if we were to learn of any sort of engineered pathogen.”

“In the short term, what I'd really like to see is a hand-in-glove approach between Russia and the World Health Organization. That would tell us a lot. I want to know what tests were administered to the lab worker. What were the results of those tests? You know, if this were the plague, that would actually assuage a lot of my concerns because we all know how to deal with the plague. We've been dealing with the plague for hundreds of years. Even, even pneumonic plague is something that, because it has a relatively short incubation period, we know precisely how to intervene. If it's something else, then that, that is the concern that I think a lot of people are expressing.”

matches.text:
WASHINGTON – Yesterday, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper called out Trump administration policies that are increasing costs across the Denver Metro area. He stopped at Aurora’s Ahorra Mucho Supermercado for a roundtable discussion with grocers and locals about the impact of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) cuts and rising grocery prices. He then spoke to Coloradans in Globeville struggling with rising energy bills as a result of supply-chain disruptions from the War in Iran.

In Aurora, Hickenlooper toured Ahorra Mucho before sitting down with local grocers and community members to discuss grocery prices, which are up over 4% since the beginning of 2025, with some items like beef and coffee up over 16%. The group also discussed the impacts of Republican SNAP cuts resulting from the ‘One Big Beautiful Bill Act’ passed last year.

Hickenlooper has been a staunch opponent of Republican SNAP cuts, which have kicked 34,000 Coloradans off SNAP, including 13,000 children. He has led the charge against new provisions that require states to spend more of their state budgets to cover SNAP benefits and administrative costs associated with them.

In Denver, Hickenlooper hosted a discussion with residents and energy assistance leaders to hear how soaring energy bills are hitting Colorado families, as Trump’s Iran war and growing demand push costs higher. Residents voiced concerns about footing the bill for data centers and electricity costs continuing to rise right as Coloradans struggle with growing inflation.

Hickenlooper noted his strong support for full funding levels for energy assistance programs like the Low Income Home Energy Affordability Program (LIHEAP), which provides funding for Colorado’s Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP). He also spoke about the need to shield ratepayers from paying for Big Tech’s data center infrastructure.

Washington, DC – U.S. Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) sent two letters last week opposing the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) proposal to eliminate the 30-day mandatory public notice period that allows communities to provide input on proposed facilities, like data centers, that may affect the air they breathe.

The first letter urges EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin to withdraw the proposed rule and disclose any documents showing that the agency communicated with data center owners ahead of the proposal.

“We agree that permitting should be efficient, predictable, and capable of supporting theinfrastructure our country needs. But faster permitting should not come at the expense of transparency or communities’ ability to shape the decisions that affect them,” wrote the senators to Administrator Zeldin.

The second letter calls on nine major data center companies – Anthropic, AWS, Fermi, Google, Joule, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and xAI – to commit to maintaining current public participation standards regardless of the rule’s outcome. The senators asked the companies to explain their own policies governing community engagement before constructing data centers and disclose any documents showing that the companies communicated with EPA, the White House, or other federal agencies ahead of the proposal.

“Data center companies like yours…have a responsibility not to use weaker requirements to limit…communities’ ability to meaningfully shape decisions that affect them,” wrote the senators to the data center companies.“America can build the infrastructure needed to compete and innovate while keeping communities informed and involved in the decisions that affect them.”

The senators requested both parties provide relevant documents and answers to their questions by October 23, 2026.

In addition to Whitehouse and Kelly, the letter to the EPA was co-signed by Senators Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Edward Markey (D-MA), and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

In addition to Whitehouse and Kelly, the letter to the data companies was co-signed by Senators Ron Wyden (D-OR), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

Read the full letter to the EPA here.

matches.text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) introduced H.Res. 1611, a bipartisan resolution designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day."

"Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are an important part of America’s energy future,” said Congressman Costa. "By investing in American innovation, we can strengthen our energy security, build a more reliable and resilient grid, create good-paying jobs, and reduce emissions. The United States has long been a leader in developing these technologies, and this bipartisan resolution recognizes the work being done across the country to ensure we continue leading the way."

"Connecticut continues to lead the nation as a hub for the research and development of clean hydrogen and fuel cell technologies," said Congressman Larson. "For years, I have worked across the aisle to enact tax incentives to boost hydrogen production and invest federal funding to grow our fuel cell economy, unleash the power of American-made clean energy, and reduce emissions. As we recognize the twelfth annual National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day, we must work together on real solutions to lower costs for consumers and grow the clean energy supply chain across the country."

"Supporting clean hydrogen unlocks a wealth of benefits — boosting our economy, protecting energy security, and reducing emissions," Congressman Tonko said. "Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve worked to advance legislation that invests in energy innovation and lowers costs, which is why I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce this bipartisan resolution and support a stronger, healthier, more competitive nation."

"I’m proud to join my colleagues in reintroducing a bipartisan resolution designating October 8th as National Hydrogen Fuel Cell Day. Advancing these technologies is critical to strengthening our nation’s energy independence, driving continued innovation, and enhancing our energy security. An all-of-the-above energy strategy will help lower energy costs for Central Valley communities while ensuring our farms, businesses, and homes have access to the reliable energy they need to thrive," said Congressman Valadao.

"The question is not whether America will need more energy—it is whether we will lead in producing it. Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies can strengthen our energy security, reinforce the reliability and resilience of our grid, create good-paying American jobs, and help meet growing demand through cleaner, innovative solutions. National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day recognizes the incredible scientists, engineers, manufacturers, and workers driving that progress, and reaffirms our bipartisan commitment to ensuring America continues to lead the world in energy innovation," said Congressman Fitzpatrick.

"Congress has long recognized how hydrogen seamlessly fits into so many of the energy tools in America’s energy portfolio," said Frank Wolak, President and CEO of FCHEA. "Whether a feedstock for low-carbon fertilizer and export fuels such as ammonia or used directly as a fuel on its own to power data centers, heavy-duty trucks, and everything in between, hydrogen helps the U.S. meet growing power demand at home while sustaining leadership in energy markets abroad. We thank Representative Costa and the resolution’s co-sponsors for supporting Hydrogen Day and the U.S. industry at large."

BACKGROUND

National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day is observed annually on October 8 in recognition of hydrogen’s atomic mass of 1.008. The day highlights the role hydrogen and fuel cell technologies play in American energy production, transportation, grid reliability, and economic growth.

The United States produces and uses approximately 10 million metric tons of hydrogen each year. Hydrogen can be derived from a variety of domestic resources and used to store energy, while fuel cell technologies are used for transportation, stationary power, and backup power.

U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) are co-leads of the House Resolution, with Representatives Mike Lawler (NY-17), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joining as original co-sponsors.
